introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 3 (0750), Paper 3, ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2023. Time allowed: three and a quarter hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR QUESTIONS in all. Answer question ONE and three others, choosing ONE question from SECTION B and TWO from SECTION C. Question ONE carries thirty-one marks and the rest carry twenty-three marks each. Only the required number of questions will be marked.

In answering questions on this paper, you are encouraged to refer to your own field and practical work where relevant. Credit will be awarded for such references. Candidates are advised NOT to attempt the questions on field investigations if such an exercise has not been carried out.

Marks will be awarded for well annotated maps and diagrams where these are relevant. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Calculators are allowed. Materials required: Topographic map, Graph Paper and Two outline maps of Cameroon.
incertitudes: Règle de choix : le sujet impose « Answer FOUR questions in all : question ONE (obligatoire, 31 marks), ONE question de la Section B et TWO de la Section C ». `regles_choix` porte le minimum exprimable par section (B : 1 sur 2 ; C : 2 sur 4) ; la question 1 (Section A) est obligatoire donc sans règle ; la consigne complète (4 questions en tout) est recopiée dans `introduction_markdown`.

Points : Q1 = 31 (5+6+4+4+6+4+2), Q2 à Q7 = 23 chacune (Q2 : 4+2+3+4+5+3+2 ; Q3 : 12+3+5+3 ; Q4 : 5+10+8 ; Q5 : 6+(8+3)+6 ; Q6 : 6+10+7 ; Q7 : 8+6+9), soit 100 points pour les 4 questions à traiter ; aucun écart avec les totaux imprimés. Pour les blocs à plusieurs items (Q1 a, b, c ; Q5 b), `points` de la sous-question est la somme des points imprimés des items.

Sujet scanné de 5 pages (page de garde, questions 1 à 7, carte topographique de Ndop avec sa légende, fond de carte du Cameroun) ; filigranes gcerevision.com ignorés. La carte (pivotée de 90 degrés sur la page, remise à l'endroit) et le fond de carte SONT dans le PDF et ont été recadrés en PNG ; le papier millimétré n'est pas fourni.

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées au niveau Advanced Level. Aucune statistique précise n'est avancée sauf celles du tableau imprimé de la Q3 ; les ordres de grandeur (pluviométries, altitudes, dates de création d'organismes ou de lois) sont donnés prudemment et sont à faire relire par un géographe avant mise en avant.

Q1 : la carte de Ndop est un scan de qualité moyenne (basse résolution, pli central vers l'Easting 55-56, texte souvent illisible). Les descriptions (relief plus élevé et plus disséqué à l'ouest de l'Easting 56, plaine à pentes douces et terrains marécageux à l'est, escarpement hachuré vers le Northing 41 à l'ouest, route goudronnée dans le nord, symbole de rizière dans le sud-ouest de la plaine) sont lues sur le scan ; les altitudes citées (environ 1 150 à 1 200 m à l'est, plus de 1 200 m à l'ouest) sont des ordres de grandeur lus sur des cotes partiellement lisibles ; les toponymes cités (Ndop, Bamessing, Babanki Tungo, Balikumbat) sont ceux qui se lisent sur le scan ; à vérifier sur la carte originale.

Q4(c) cite UNVDA (Upper Noun Valley Development Authority), SEMRY, IRAD, CamCCUL, MINADER, les ordonnances foncières de 1974 : institutions réelles mais dates et résultats volontairement non détaillés.

questions.enonce_markdown: (a) Identify ONE highland and ONE lowland crossed by the Cameroon Volcanic Line and briefly explain the relief characteristics of the lowland. *(5 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Identification (2 marks).** The Cameroon Volcanic Line (CVL) is a chain of volcanic mountains and highlands that runs from the Gulf of Guinea (the coast and the offshore islands) north-eastwards through the south-west and the west of Cameroon to the north.
- *Highland:* **Mount Cameroon** (the highest point, a still active volcano), or the **Bamenda Highlands / Mount Oku**, the Bamboutos Mountains, or Mount Manengouba.
- *Lowland:* the **Ndop Plain** (in the Bamenda Highlands), or the Tikar Plain, or the Mbo Plain.

**Relief characteristics of the Ndop Plain (3 marks).** (Choose the lowland named.)
1. It is a **flat to gently undulating** basin floor, at a height of about 1,100 to 1,200 m above sea level (the Ndop map shows spot heights of this order), lower than the surrounding highlands. *(1 mark)*
2. It is **surrounded by higher ground** (the Bamenda Highlands and Mount Oku, with steep slopes and escarpments) and is believed to be an old lake basin or a basin formed by faulting and volcanic damming, which was filled with alluvium. *(1 mark)*
3. The floor is drained by the **River Noun and its tributaries**, which flow slowly and meander; the low gradient causes seasonal flooding and **extensive swamps** and alluvial flats, with a few rounded low hills and inselbergs rising out of the plain. *(1 mark)*

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) Illustrate how the physical environment has influenced the spatial pattern of food crop farming systems in Cameroon. *(10 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Approach.** Show that the type of crop and the farming system depend on the physical conditions (climate, relief, soils, water), which change from the south to the north and with altitude; illustrate each with a zone, the crops and the farming system (a sketch map of the zones earns credit).

**1. The humid forest zone of the south (equatorial climate, South, Centre, East, Littoral, South-West).** *(2 marks)*
- Very high rainfall (often more than 1,500 mm a year) in two seasons and high temperatures; deep but leached ferrallitic soils.
- Crops: **cassava, cocoyam, yams, plantain and banana**, maize, groundnuts and vegetables; the system is **shifting cultivation or bush fallow** and mixed cropping, because the soils lose fertility quickly when the forest is cleared.

**2. The Western Highlands and the volcanic slopes (Bamenda, West).** *(2 marks)*
- Cooler temperatures at altitude, plentiful rain and **fertile volcanic soils**; the high population density.
- Crops: **maize, beans, Irish potatoes, vegetables and cocoyam**, with intensive mixed farming, small plots, terracing on the steep slopes, manuring and crop rotation.

**3. The flat, waterlogged plains (for example, the Ndop plain; the Logone flood plain in the Far North).** *(2 marks)*
- Alluvial soils, high water table and flooding: **rice** is grown in paddy fields or irrigated schemes (UNVDA in the Ndop plain; SEMRY in the Logone area); on the better-drained margins vegetables are grown.

**4. The Adamawa plateau and the Guinea savanna.** *(1 mark)* Moderate altitude and a single rainy season, tall grass: maize, yams, cassava and groundnuts on small farms, with extensive cattle grazing.

**5. The northern savanna (Sudan and Sahel zones).** *(2 marks)* Low and short, unreliable rainfall (a single rainy season of about 4 to 6 months), a long dry season and the dry Harmattan: drought-resistant **sorghum, millet, groundnuts and cowpeas**; on the clay soils the dry-season sorghum (muskuwaari) uses the water stored in the soil; irrigation along rivers.

**6. Relief and soils in general.** *(1 mark)* Steep slopes limit the land that can be cultivated and need terraces; the valley bottoms with water are used for rice and dry-season vegetables, and the interfluves for tubers and cereals.

**Conclusion.** The result is a **zonal, north to south pattern** of crops (cereals in the north, tubers and bananas in the south), modified by relief and altitude in the highlands, which is why Cameroon is called "Africa in miniature".

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) Discuss TWO socio-economic factors that hinder agricultural development in Cameroon and bring out the respective measures that have been put in place to solve the problems. *(8 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan (4 marks per factor: 2 for the discussion and 2 for the measures).**

**Factor 1 - Lack of capital and credit, and poor access to inputs.**
- *Discussion:* most farmers are smallholders with low incomes. They cannot buy fertilisers, improved seeds, pesticides and tools, and banks regard them as high-risk borrowers without collateral, so they continue to use the hoe and the cutlass, and the yields and the farm size remain small.
- *Measures:* the creation of **farmers' groups, cooperatives and Common Initiative Groups (CIGs)** to obtain loans and inputs; **microfinance** institutions such as the credit unions (CamCCUL) and community credit networks; government subsidies for fertiliser and improved seeds; the research and extension support of **IRAD** and the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (MINADER) which supplies improved varieties and advice.

**Factor 2 - Poor transport and marketing.**
- *Discussion:* many production areas are connected by poor earth feeder roads, which become impassable in the rains. The transport cost is high, perishable crops (tomatoes, plantain, vegetables) rot before they reach the town, the middlemen fix low prices and the storage and processing facilities are inadequate. The farmers are discouraged from producing a surplus.
- *Measures:* the construction and rehabilitation of rural roads and bridges, rural markets and storage facilities; the encouragement of cooperatives to sell collectively and of small processing units; the government development agencies such as the UNVDA (rice in Ndop) and SEMRY (rice in the Far North) have organised production and marketing.

**Other acceptable factors:** land tenure problems and land fragmentation (measure: the 1974 land ordinances, land registration and the creation of agro-industrial estates), rural exodus and an ageing farm population (measure: youth farming programmes), and illiteracy.

**Conclusion.** These measures have had mixed results because of limited funding, corruption and weak implementation, so farmers' incomes remain low.
